suspicions.claim: The basic auth error handler now returns 'name' instead of 'message' in the JSON error response, breaking the documented error format.
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/tokens with invalid Basic Auth credentials (e.g., Authorization: Basic invalid). Read the JSON response body and verify the error object contains 'name' instead of the documented 'message' field.
suspicions.evidence: POST /api/tokens with invalid Basic Auth returned 401 with 'message' in base and 'name' in head (f14, f15, f19).

suspicions.claim: The basic auth error handler still returns the 'WWW-Authenticate': 'Form' header but the error body format changed, potentially breaking clients expecting the documented 'message' field with that header.
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/tokens with invalid Basic Auth credentials. Read the response headers for 'WWW-Authenticate' and the JSON body for 'name' vs 'message' field.
suspicions.evidence: Probes for s2 did not include response headers, so presence of 'WWW-Authenticate' header cannot be verified.

suspicions.claim: The token auth error handler now returns 'name' instead of 'message' in the JSON error response, breaking the documented error format for token authentication failures.
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/users with an invalid or missing Bearer token (Authorization: Bearer invalid). Read the JSON response body and verify the error object contains 'name' instead of the documented 'message' field.
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/users with invalid Bearer token returned 401 with 'message' in base and 'name' in head (f16, f17, f18).

suspicions.claim: The token auth error handler no longer returns the 'WWW-Authenticate' header that basic auth returns, creating an inconsistency between auth error responses that clients may rely on.
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/users with an invalid Bearer token. Compare response headers with a failed Basic Auth request to /api/tokens; observe missing 'WWW-Authenticate' header in token auth error response.
suspicions.evidence: Probes for s4 did not include response headers, so presence or absence of 'WWW-Authenticate' header cannot be verified.
